goals: PRIMARY (requested): compute hillslope-to-stream travel times including lateral flow convergence and inter-hillslope groundwater exchange
FALLBACK (feasible precursor only): characterize vertical recharge/drainage flux across topographic positions as boundary fluxes for a future routing/coupled model
key_processes: lateral saturated/unsaturated flow along topographic flowpaths
groundwater exchange between neighboring hillslope positions
flowpath travel-time integration to the stream network
vertical recharge/drainage partitioning (the only piece the stack can produce)

model_choice.rationale: ELM is single-column 1-D with no lateral transport, no routing, and no regional water table. The question's core mechanism (lateral convergence, inter-column groundwater exchange, travel time) is outside what the stack can represent. ELM can only produce independent vertical fluxes.
model_choice.coupling_note: Even ELM->PFLOTRAN weak coupling (unbuilt) would not answer this: PFLOTRAN here is steady-state groundwater and one-way weak coupling passes only a recharge-flux BC. Hillslope-to-stream travel times require transient connected-mesh flow with particle tracking and a routing layer, plus two-way groundwater exchange — none of which exists.

answerable: vertical recharge/drainage flux (QDRAI) and soil-moisture profile at individual topographic positions
how vertical partitioning differs between valley-bottom, mid-slope, and ridge columns under elevation-varied NLDAS forcing and position-specific soils

not_answerable.why: single-column ELM has no lateral transport and no routing; travel time requires connected flowpath integration the stack cannot perform
not_answerable.needs: transient connected-domain flow model with flowpath/particle tracking and a routing layer

not_answerable.aspect: lateral flow convergence along topographic flowpaths
not_answerable.why: columns are independent 1-D points with no column-to-column exchange, so convergence cannot occur
not_answerable.needs: laterally coupled subsurface model (e.g. ParFlow / integrated hydrology) or an ELM lateral-flow scheme

not_answerable.aspect: groundwater exchange between neighboring hillslope positions
not_answerable.why: no regional/lateral groundwater flow; each column cold-starts/equilibrates its own 1-D water table
not_answerable.needs: two-way lateral groundwater coupling between columns

sampling_strategy.approach: stratified by topographic position (fallback recharge characterization only — NOT a travel-time design)

classes: dominant SSURGO classes sampled per topographic band

sampling_strategy.n_justification: 4 topographic-position bands spanning 352-1977 m x up to ~3 dominant soils per band, lightly reduced, gives ~12 independent vertical columns. This spans the topographic gradient for the FALLBACK recharge-flux characterization; it does NOT and cannot resolve the requested lateral/travel-time mechanism.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Concentrate along representative hillslope transects from ridge to valley bottom so per-position vertical fluxes could later feed a coupled routing model; oversample valley-bottom/riparian positions where groundwater-soil-moisture exchange would be strongest in a future coupled setup.
sampling_strategy.replication: Light: one column per (band x dominant soil) combination; no replication needed since these are deterministic 1-D points and the design is a precursor, not the answer.

sampling_plan.reason: Vertical recharge/drainage and shallowest water table; oversampled because this is where lateral exchange would dominate in a future coupled model (fallback flux only).
Transitional vertical flux regime between hillslope and valley; characterizes the down-gradient recharge boundary for a future coupler.
Mid-hillslope vertical partitioning under intermediate elevation forcing and soils.
Highest-elevation recharge source area; NLDAS gives distinct orographic precip/temperature here for the vertical flux estimate.

validation_design.comparison: none — no observations exist in-domain and the model cannot produce this variable

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: elevation-varied NLDAS forcing (1980-2018), per-position SSURGO soil, WTD-informed warm start + spin-up years (recharge/water-table target requires it) — produces vertical fluxes only, NOT travel times

requires_capabilities.capability: laterally coupled subsurface flow (column-to-column exchange, e.g. ParFlow/integrated hydrology or an ELM lateral-flow scheme)
requires_capabilities.why: the requested convergence and inter-hillslope groundwater exchange are inherently lateral
requires_capabilities.blocks: lateral flow convergence and neighbor groundwater exchange

requires_capabilities.capability: flowpath / particle tracking and travel-time integration over a connected domain
requires_capabilities.why: hillslope-to-stream travel time is a transport-time quantity along connected flowpaths
to connect hillslope positions to the stream network
requires_capabilities.blocks: hillslope-to-stream connectivity and integrated flux to gages

requires_capabilities.why: would let ELM vertical QDRAI drive a groundwater model as a precursor; still one-way and steady-state, insufficient for travel time
requires_capabilities.blocks: even the partial coupled precursor is not yet runnable

requires_capabilities.capability: DEM-derived hillslope/flowpath delineation and topographic-position classification
requires_capabilities.why: to define ridge/slope/valley strata and flowpaths for the expander and any future routing

requires_capabilities.capability: model spin-up / WTD-informed warm start for recharge and water-table targets
requires_capabilities.why: recharge and water table are slow states; cold-start default 8.8 m water table makes them artifacts
requires_capabilities.blocks: meaningful vertical recharge/drainage in the fallback

assumptions: Naches is inside CONUS, so NLDAS-2 0.125 deg forcing applies and gives elevation-varying precipitation/temperature across the 352-1977 m range.
No in-domain observations were provided, so no validation of any product is possible.
The fallback vertical-flux design is offered only as a precursor for a future coupled/routing capability; it does not answer the travel-time question as posed.
Topographic-position strata will be delineated deterministically downstream from a DEM; no coordinates are specified here.
open_questions: Is the true goal a lateral-flow / travel-time study (which needs a laterally coupled model outside this stack), or would per-position vertical recharge fluxes be an acceptable interim deliverable?
Is there any observational target (streamflow gage, well network, tracer/age data) in the Naches to validate travel times, or would this be purely mechanistic?
Is adopting an integrated-hydrology model (ParFlow/ParFlow-CONUS2) or building ELM lateral-flow coupling in scope, since the request is not answerable without it?
